raw_response:
I’m 47 this year, and with 70 mu I can’t farm like the very small households anymore, but I also can’t throw money around like the big operators. I’ve only done this 6 years, so I still lean a lot on what I’ve seen in my own fields and what the better farmers nearby do. I finished middle school, so I do pay attention when the extension people talk about split fertilizer and timing, but in the end I still decide by what the crop looks like and what I can afford. Since I have a well, I’m not as passive as farmers waiting only on rain, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the crop is at a key stage.

For the main land, I’ll keep wheat-maize on 35 mu because that’s the safest income pattern here. Wheat is already in the field, so now I’ll manage it through jointing and grain filling, then rush into summer maize right after harvest. On the other 35 mu I’ll spread risk with cotton, watermelon, chili, and cauliflower. Watermelon and chili bring cash if the market is good, but they need more labor and more pesticide watching. Cotton is slower but steadier. Cauliflower gives me another vegetable crop, but I won’t make it too big because it is labor-heavy and prices can swing fast. I’m not chasing the highest yield on every mu. I’d rather keep fertilizer at a level that usually works, leave some cash for irrigation and spray, and make sure I can actually manage the fields on time.
